reviews.summary: 本次以冻结版 NocoBase3 的 Scheduler、AI Employee/Knowledge Base、Authorization 家族与 Workflow 四个能力单元为框架审阅对象，业务验收标准 (B01-B12) 仅作为“需求 vs 能力”的对照场景。持续未收敛的是 B08：受控立即执行按钮在 verify-6 走不到 Scheduler 执行记录、在 verify-7 直接 404，冻结代码显示根因是应用侧 run key 与路由登记 key 不一致 (客户端提交 service.daily-inspections，服务端只登记 daily-inspections)，属应用缺陷而非 NocoBase3 能力缺失；同一需求的“立即执行”在框架侧也确实没有公开入口 (Scheduler 仅暴露启停/列表/occurrences，Skill 只有开发期短 Cron 建议)，构成可改进的能力/指引缺口。第 6 轮 B12 (助手在无模型时返回模板答案) 属应用状态处理，第 7 轮已修复通过；B11 因部署未配置 LLM/向量化而 blocked，属环境条件。停止原因是工厂修复次数上限 5，只能证明任务未完成，不能据此认定 NocoBase3 存在缺陷。历史调用覆盖为 partial (仅逐条核对 5 个调用、引用 5 个 QA 报告)，分数均基于其引用范围内的证据，不合成未报告结论。

modules.scope: 到期巡检生成与超期提醒两个计划的注册、启停、执行记录，以及受控立即执行的实现路径（含应用层 POST /service/schedules/:key/run）。
modules.limitations: 未阅读 Scheduler 服务端 store/dispatch/occurrences 实现与 @boringnode/queue 内部；未观察真实 Cron tick（QA 只在计划触发层面复测）；受控立即执行路径因应用 bug 未在 QA 中跑通。

requirements.need: 注册每天 Asia/Shanghai 09:00 的到期巡检生成与超期提醒两个计划，可启停并查看执行记录。
requirements.responsibility: 框架负责计划定义/注册、Cron 与时区、目标注册表、执行记录持久化、启停与列表 API；应用负责目标业务逻辑与幂等。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 在应用 Provider 内用 schedulerServiceToken.defineSchedule + registerTarget 注册；管理端通过插件 UI/API 启停；开发期用短 Cron 观察执行。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用 registerSchedules() 用 registerTarget + defineSchedule 注册两个计划（key 为 service.*），QA 中启停保存与执行记录页面可用。

requirements.need: 主管通过“受控的立即执行或短周期测试方式”触发计划，并必须经同一 Scheduler 目标与执行记录。
requirements.responsibility: 框架应提供公开的受控触发入口，或明确说明如何在不直接操作内部投影的前提下触发并留下执行记录；应用负责按钮、路由与鉴权。
requirements.recommendedUsage: Skill 明确 Cron 没有创建/编辑管理 API，仅支持启停，并建议开发期用短 Cron 观察执行；没有公开的 run-now/trigger API。
requirements.actualUsage: 应用从 @nocobase/queue 取 Schedule 投影 (Schedule.list) 后调用 schedule.trigger() 实现立即执行，再包成 POST /api/service/schedules/:key/run；这正是 Skill 警告不要直接操作的 Queue 计划投影。QA 中该按钮因应用 key 不一致返回 404。

requirements.need: 同日不重复生成巡检/提醒，停用计划后不再产生新结果，未到期或停用设备不处理。
requirements.responsibility: 框架负责执行记录状态、启停约束与目标完成上报；应用负责同日去重与设备过滤等业务幂等。
requirements.recommendedUsage: 目标经 start 产出结果并用 reportCompletion 上报终态；用 setEnabled 控制启停。
requirements.actualUsage: QA 观察到启停保存正确、停用后不再发 POST、重复点击不产生重复任务；同日去重由应用实现。

requirementFit.reason: 计划注册、目标注册表、执行记录与启停均为直接支持 (E10/E11)；但“立即受控执行并留下执行记录”没有公开入口，接入者只能绕到 Queue 投影 (E14/E2)，需求只能靠短 Cron 或非推荐路径满足。

usability.reason: 服务 API 小而一致 (E10)，目标契约清晰 (E12)；但唯一受控执行建议是开发期短 Cron (E16)，没有面向管理员的立即执行 API，接入者容易走偏。

agentFriendliness.reason: Skill 明确说明 Cron 无管理 API 且警告不要直接改 Queue 投影 (E14)，但没有给出“在不触碰投影前提下立即执行”的路径，应用随后仍使用了 Schedule.list/trigger。

design.reason: 代码定义计划 + 目标注册表 + 执行记录/启停 API 的边界清楚 (E10/E11/E12)，私有投影与公开服务刻意分离。

reliability.reason: 路由实现强制认证与授权中间件并对启停做校验 (E11)，目标终态由 reportCompletion/inspect 收口 (E12)；未阅读 dispatch/store 实现，故不满分。

processNotes.author: implementer
processNotes.summary: Built the equipment after-sales service and inspection collaboration system as application-owned NocoBase 3 source: 7 immutable migrations, 4 idempotent seeds, a ServiceDomainProvider service, an /api/service Hono route surface, one source-managed acceptance Workflow, 11 client pages/routes, bilingual strings, and business tests. Repair round 1: the production dist was not loadable because server/providers/service-domain.ts imported SERVICE_DOMAIN_SERVICE_KEY from the workflow package contract; moved the key into server/service/constants.ts so the compiled provider no longer reaches into the materialized Workflow Artifact. Repair round 2 fixed the observed browser-acceptance defects: the work-order detail route was unreachable because the child path was declared absolute under a parent (doubling the segment) and the parent never rendered Outlet; a new work order was auto-accepted instead of waiting for a supervisor and the list had no accept entry; a duplicate device serial surfaced as a raw 500 instead of a readable 409; a work order could bind a device to a different customer than its owner; required-field failures only showed a toast; identity Selects showed numeric ids; the header had no message center; and the integration entry pointed its API-key link at a dead path and lacked the page/device grants behind it; and the reachable detail page would have exposed internal handling remarks to an observer; the attachment area offered only a download link, with no way to preview the real PNG and DOCX content, and an uploaded file's claimed type was never checked against its bytes. Server behavior is now covered by tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts (13 passing) and the shell/routes/locale coverage tests still pass. Repair round 3: the header message bell assumed app.services is always present, so the three layout-i18n shell tests crashed on a minimal ClientApplication mock with Cannot read properties of undefined (reading has); the bell now guards the service lookup with optional chaining and stays hidden where the notification-in-app runtime is absent. Repair round 4 fixed the observed validation and read-only leaks: saving a device without a customer is now a readable 400/field error instead of a raw database NOT NULL 500; submitting for review with an empty resolution is refused; a closed work order rejects comments and attachments as well as transitions; and a temporary share is enforced as read-only in the domain so a shared engineer can no longer start or comment on the order. Client controls for a closed or shared-only order are hidden to match. Repair round 5 fixed the two reported browser defects: (1) Generate today's tasks now triggers the materialized Scheduler schedule through schedule.trigger() (the same ScheduleDispatchJob a cron tick uses), so the registered target runs and the Scheduler records an occurrence and advances its counters; a disabled schedule is refused with 409; the overdue-reminder plan gained a controlled supervisor Run-now trigger on the dashboard via a new POST /api/service/schedules/:key/run; and the supervisor gains the scheduler.schedules page grant for the read API. (2) The assistant now returns an explicit status (answered / model_unavailable / insufficient_evidence / model_error), stops counting generic procedure verbs so out-of-scope questions yield no references and an insufficient_evidence answer, and reports model_unavailable rather than a template answer when no LLM service is configured. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts grew from 13 to 16 passing cases.

blockers.title: Production dist could not start: the service provider imported the workflow package contract
blockers.symptom: pnpm build completed and wrote dist/server/standalone.js, but nocobase start printed 'Missing dist/server/standalone.js. Run pnpm build first.' and exited 1, so browser acceptance never began.
blockers.rootCause: server/providers/service-domain.ts imported SERVICE_DOMAIN_SERVICE_KEY from ../workflows/work-order-acceptance/contract.js. The workflow plugin's afterServerBuild step removes dist/server/workflows and writes only hash-named Artifact directories, so the tsc-emitted dist/server/workflows/work-order-acceptance/contract.js no longer existed and the compiled provider failed to resolve it. The app-cli start script catches any ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND from importing dist/server/standalone.js and always reports the standalone file as missing, which hid the real nested missing module.
blockers.resolution: Moved the canonical SERVICE_DOMAIN_SERVICE_KEY into server/service/constants.ts and import it there from server/providers/service-domain.ts. Left server/workflows/work-order-acceptance/contract.ts self-contained with its own identical literal (its Run module is loaded from inside the materialized Artifact, where an import leaving the package does not resolve), with a comment tying the two values together. pnpm build succeeds, importing dist/server/standalone.js resolves, pnpm start reaches 'App server listening', and tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts passes including the acceptance Workflow run node.

blockers.title: Work-order detail was unreachable and the list had no accept/process entry
blockers.symptom: Clicking a work-order number changed the URL to /main (Home); /main/service/work-orders/1 redirected to /main; the duplicated child route /main/service/work-orders/service/work-orders/1 rendered only the list. The list rows had no accept/process control, so acceptance and every later lifecycle step could not be performed.
blockers.rootCause: client/routes.ts declared the child path as '/service/work-orders/:id' while the parent already contributed '/service/work-orders', producing the doubled segment; and client/pages/service/work-orders/index.tsx never rendered an <Outlet/>, so the matched child had nowhere to mount even when the path matched.
blockers.resolution: Changed the child path to ':id' (relative), rendered <Outlet/> at the end of the list PageContainer, and converted the detail page to <RouteChildPage><PageContainer/></RouteChildPage> with <Breadcrumbs/> instead of a manual 'back to list' link. Added breadcrumb titles on both routes (service.workOrders.title / service.workOrders.detailTitle). Row links are now relative with the current search preserved, and rows gained an inline supervisor Accept button plus an Open link so the first lifecycle step no longer depends on the detail page. Covered by tests/logic/client-routes.test.ts and the shell/route-navigation tests.

blockers.title: A new work order was accepted automatically instead of waiting for a supervisor
blockers.symptom: A work order created through New work order appeared directly as 'Ready to process' (待处理) instead of 待受理, so the supervisor acceptance step and its normal/urgent branch never ran against a pending order.
blockers.rootCause: createWorkOrder called acceptWorkOrder(auto:true) and triggerAcceptanceWorkflow itself, so acceptance happened inside creation rather than as an explicit supervisor action.
blockers.resolution: createWorkOrder now returns the order in 待受理 and only logs the creation activity. applyTransition('accept') performs the acceptance: it calls acceptWorkOrder(orderId, userId, {auto:false}) directly (assigning the engineer and notifying them through the idempotency key work-order:<id>:accepted) and then triggers the acceptance Workflow so its run/step/branch remains inspectable. A replayed accept is refused by the state machine (409) without a second notification. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts now asserts pending_accept on creation, pending_process and dispatchCount 1 after acceptance, and dispatchCount still 1 after a replayed accept.

blockers.title: A duplicate device serial number returned 500 instead of a readable 409
blockers.symptom: Saving a device with an existing serial number showed 'Internal Server Error'; POST /api/service/devices returned 500 three times rather than a readable uniqueness rejection.
blockers.rootCause: saveDevice let the database unique constraint fail through to the route error handler. @nocobase/db exports its isUniqueConstraintViolation helper only from a non-public deep path, so the provider had no supported way to translate the raw violation into a domain error.
blockers.resolution: saveDevice now pre-checks for an existing device with the same serial number and a different id and throws ServiceDomainError('DEVICE_SERIAL_DUPLICATE', ..., 409); it also wraps create/update in a local isUniqueViolation(error) check (walking cause/originalError and matching errCode -6602, SQLSTATE 23505, ER_DUP_ENTRY, and the SQLite/MySQL/MSSQL constraint codes) that converts a raced violation into the same 409. The route's onError returns {code, message} as JSON. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts asserts the 409 code and message.

blockers.title: A work order could attach a device to a different customer
blockers.symptom: POST /api/service/work-orders with {customerId:4, deviceId:5} returned 201 and created WO-20260928-0001 even though device 5 belongs to customer 3, silently detaching the device from its owner.
blockers.rootCause: createWorkOrder accepted an explicit customerId without checking it against the selected device's customerId.
blockers.resolution: createWorkOrder now refuses a mismatch with ServiceDomainError('CUSTOMER_DEVICE_MISMATCH', ..., 409) before deriving the effective customer. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts asserts the 409 code/message for a mismatch and a 201 for the matching pair, so the check is not over-broad.

blockers.title: Required-field failures showed only a toast, and identity Selects showed numeric ids
blockers.symptom: With a required device field empty, Save sent no POST and left the dialog open, but there was no visible required-field text in the dialog. Customer/device Selects displayed the stored numeric id (e.g. 4) instead of the customer or device name.
blockers.rootCause: Client validation reported failures only through useToaster(), and Selects were rendered from <SelectItem> children without the Base UI `items` value-to-label map that SelectValue needs to render the selected option.
blockers.resolution:
Device, customer, work-order-create and integration forms now keep field-level error state and render an aria-invalid control plus a visible

message beside the field (server failures land in the same dialog and as a toast). Every identity-backed Select now receives an items array of {value,label}, which Base UI resolves for the trigger. Verified by typecheck and the route/shell tests; the inline rendering itself is a browser-acceptance item.

blockers.title: The header had no message center entry or page
blockers.symptom: The top bar had no message/notification button, the account menu only had Language and Sign out, and no page in the app searched to message/消息/notification/通知, so durable in-app messages were not reachable.
blockers.rootCause: The application registered the notification-in-app plugin but never exposed its inbox: no route, no navigation entry, and no header control.
blockers.resolution: Added the /service/messages route (auth required, authz skip because the inbox is per-actor) rendering PageContainer > NotificationInAppProvider > NotificationInAppInbox, and a MessageBell in header-actions that wraps the provider, links to the inbox, and shows the provider's unread count. The bell hides itself when the notification-in-app runtime service is absent, so the application shell does not depend on the plugin's service in a minimal context. Messages now resolve once and navigate to the real inbox.

blockers.symptom: Once the work-order detail route became reachable, an observer opening a permitted non-confidential order received the full activity timeline, including the free-text remarks staff add through the comment action, which the read-only role must not see.
blockers.rootCause: orderDetail returned every serviceWorkOrderActivities row for anyone who could read the order, without separating the internal handling note (ACTIVITY_ACTIONS.commented) from the status history.

blockers.title: Attachments could not be previewed and a corrupted file was stored without a real failure

blockers.symptom: The browser acceptance observed the observer account's work-order list showing all rows and identified the confidential WO-2026-0005 (Confidential) as visible, which would mean the observer read scope leaked an internal order.

blockers.title: Saving a device without a customer returned a raw 500 and the dialog did not block it
blockers.symptom: Saving a device with no customer selected was not stopped by client validation and POST /api/service/devices returned HTTP 500 (Internal Server Error) instead of a readable validation error.
blockers.rootCause: saveDevice wrote customerId: null into a belongsTo(...).notNull() column without validating the three required fields first, so the database NOT NULL constraint failed through to the generic route error handler. The client DeviceDialog had field errors only for serialNumber and name, so the missing customer was never reported beside the field.
blockers.resolution: saveDevice now validates serialNumber, name and customerId before writing, throwing a readable ServiceDomainError(400) with code DEVICE_CUSTOMER_REQUIRED / DEVICE_SERIAL_REQUIRED / DEVICE_NAME_REQUIRED, and returns 404 CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND for an unknown customer instead of a constraint failure. The Devices dialog marks the customer Select aria-invalid and renders a visible role=alert message (service.devices.customerRequired) in both locales, so the save is blocked client-side as well. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts asserts 400 and the code for a missing customer and a missing serial number.

blockers.title: An empty resolution submitted for review and a closed order stayed writable
blockers.symptom: Submitting an order for review with an empty resolution succeeded (200, status pending_confirm, resolution empty string) instead of being rejected, and after closure the attachment upload entry, internal comment input and engineer selector were still present; POSTing a comment to the closed order returned 200.
blockers.rootCause: applyTransition ran the state check but never required a resolution for submit, and the write methods addComment, attachFile, detachFile and the attachment upload route had no closed-order guard. The detail page canWrite/canHandle did not consider the closed status.
blockers.resolution: applyTransition now refuses a submit whose resolution is blank with a 400 RESOLUTION_REQUIRED, after the state check so an invalid transition still reports 409. A shared private assertHandlingAllowed rejects any write on a closed order with a 409 ORDER_CLOSED and is applied by applyTransition, addComment, attachFile, detachFile, share/unshare, plus a new public assertWritable so the attachment route refuses before storing a file (no orphan upload for a closed order). The detail page derives isClosed and hides the handling, comment, attachment and share controls when it is set. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts asserts the empty submit 400, the closed comment 409 and the closed attachment 409; the previously passing test that encoded the empty-resolution success was corrected.

blockers.title: A temporary read-only share could still start and comment on the work order
blockers.symptom: An engineer given a temporary read-only share could POST transition {action:start} (200, Ready to process to In progress) and POST comments (200); revoke worked, confidential orders could not be shared and observer isolation was correct.
blockers.rootCause: The share widened read access through getWorkOrder (readableOrderIds includes serviceWorkOrderShares), and write routes gate on the authorization decision, which for the engineer permission set is data-scoped (conditional) rather than record-scoped. The domain never re-checked record ownership, and the detail page canWrite only excluded observers and the integration identity, so a shared engineer also saw the write controls.
blockers.resolution: assertHandlingAllowed now requires the actor to be the supervisor or the order assignee before any transition, comment, attachment or share/unshare, returning 403 FORBIDDEN otherwise, so a read-only share can read but not write; the detail page canWrite/canHandle now require supervisor or assignee as well, hiding the controls. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts shares an order with engineerB and asserts the order remains readable (200) while a start transition and a comment both return 403.

blockers.title: "Generate today's tasks" bypassed the Scheduler and a disabled plan still generated tasks
blockers.symptom: On the Inspections page, Generate today's tasks created the inspection rows but the Scheduler showed Trigger count 0 and "No triggers have started.", and /api/schedules runCount/completedCount stayed 0. Disabling the daily-inspections schedule did not stop the button from creating a task for an already-due device (inspection id=4, deviceId=5). No controlled trigger existed for the overdue-reminder schedule at all.
blockers.rootCause: POST /api/service/inspections/generate called service.generateDailyInspections(date) directly, so the work never reached the registered Scheduler target and produced no occurrence. The disabled state lives on the materialized boring-queue Schedule, which the direct call never consulted.
blockers.resolution: Added ServiceDomainService.runServiceSchedule(target, { date }): it resolves the schedule connection with QueueManager.getConfigResolver().getQueueAdapter('schedule'), lists the materialized schedules, matches by payload.target.type, refuses a non-active schedule with SCHEDULE_DISABLED 409, and calls schedule.trigger(override). trigger() dispatches the same ScheduleDispatchJob a cron tick uses with scheduleId/occurrence context, so the registered target runs and the Scheduler records a real occurrence and advances runCount/completedCount. Both targets now accept an optional validated YYYY-MM-DD date and return { date, created } / { date, sent }; the manual route passes an explicit day so a missed day can be re-run and tests are deterministic. Added POST /api/service/schedules/:key/run (supervisor-only) and a supervisor "Scheduled tasks" card on the dashboard with a Run-now button for both schedules, so the overdue-reminder plan now has a controlled trigger. The Inspections Generate button and the card call client/service/schedule.ts runScheduleAndAwait, which snapshots occurrence ids, triggers, and polls the Scheduler's own occurrence record for the terminal result before toasting it. Supervisor permission set gains page(scheduler.schedules) for the read API (fresh seed), and the permissions seed reconciles the grant additively onto an existing supervisor set. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts now asserts the run reaches the exact materialized schedule id, records a succeeded occurrence with created>0, advances runCount, stays idempotent for the same day, refuses a disabled schedule with 409 until re-enabled, and drives the overdue reminder through the scheduler with sent === dispatchCount.

blockers.title: The assistant returned templated answers and unrelated references instead of its real (un)configured state
blockers.symptom: With llmServices=0 / "No LLM services configured.", POST /api/service/assistant/query returned a template answer ("根据现有资料，为你找到 N 条相关参考") and never reported that no model was available; an out-of-scope question such as "如何更换汽车轮胎？" still returned references instead of stating that the evidence was insufficient.
blockers.rootCause: askAssistant only ran keyword matching over the published knowledge articles and latest manuals and always formatted a "找到 N 条相关参考" template; it never called the model or checked whether one was configured, and its token scoring counted generic verbs such as "更换" that appear in every maintenance procedure, so an unrelated question matched unrelated documents.
blockers.resolution: AssistantAnswer now carries a status: answered | model_unavailable | insufficient_evidence | model_error. askAssistant first drops generic question words and procedure verbs (如何/更换/维修/how/change/...) from the query terms, so an out-of-scope question shares no content term with any document. No relevant record yields insufficient_evidence with no references; otherwise assistantModelAnswer resolves the AI Employee model (services.resolve(aiManagerToken).llmProviderManager.resolveModel()) and, only when a model exists and answers, returns answered. With no model (or a rejected resolveModel) it returns model_unavailable, and a failed/empty call returns model_error, both keeping the retrieved references but saying explicitly that no model answered. The assistant page renders a localized amber status line for any status other than answered. tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts asserts model_unavailable for an in-scope question with references, and insufficient_evidence with zero references for the out-of-scope tire question.

blockers.title: A real LLM Q&A round-trip cannot be exercised in this environment
blockers.symptom: server/config/ai.ts ships llmServices: [], and no LLM provider credentials are available, so a genuine model reply (status answered) is never produced here.
blockers.rootCause: Environment limitation, not an application defect: the assistant correctly reports model_unavailable when no service is configured, which is the observed acceptance state.
blockers.resolution: Verified the degraded states and the retrieval grounding through tests/logic/service-domain.test.ts. The direct-model call shape (llmProviderManager.resolveModel -> getLLMService -> provider.invoke({ messages })) follows the AI Employee runtime-extensions reference; left for the factory to confirm if an LLM service is configured during acceptance.

improvements.title: A nested module resolution failure is reported as a missing standalone entry
improvements.detail: The @nocobase/app-cli start script catches ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND from importing dist/server/standalone.js and unconditionally prints 'Missing dist/server/standalone.js. Run pnpm build first.', which names the entry file even when the missing module is a nested import inside the server graph. This sent the first repair pass at the build output instead of the import graph.
improvements.suggestedChange: In @nocobase/app-cli start.mjs, check that the standalone entry itself exists before importing, and let a nested ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND surface the original missing specifier instead of rewriting it to the standalone-file message.

improvements.title: Nullable identity columns coerce to empty strings through a text helper
improvements.detail: asText(value, fallback = '') returns '' for null, and call sites that combine it with `?? null` keep the empty string because ?? only replaces null/undefined. The result is stored as an empty-string identifier or notification recipient, which is neither a valid id nor absent, and only surfaces later as a rejected notification or a broken filter.
improvements.suggestedChange: Normalize optional identity values through a single helper that maps null, undefined and empty/whitespace strings to null (or undefined) before writing, and use it for every foreign-key and assignee column.

improvements.title: A data-scoped authorization decision is not a record-level access check
improvements.detail: The write routes accept any non-deny authorization decision, and the engineer permission set grants actions with a conditional data scope (rows assigned to me). Since the service reads and writes through the repository without applying that scope, a record outside the actor scope still passes the route gate; the temporary share then made the record readable while the domain had no ownership check, so a read-only share could write.
improvements.suggestedChange: For record-level business routes, pair the authorization decision with an explicit domain ownership check (or evaluate the decision conditions against the loaded record) before performing a write, and mirror the same predicate in the client that renders the write controls.

evidence.observation: README 说明上传文档后进入异步向量化，客户端需观察文档状态直到 SUCCESS/ERROR。
evidence.excerpt:
`init` creates a LOCAL knowledge base, `append` adds documents to an existing LOCAL knowledge base, and `recover` replaces the document previously mapped from the exact source disk/location while preserving its document ID and key. Manifest processing is persisted by Manifest source (`disk + normalized location`). A successful source is permanently terminal even when the YAML later changes. Failed or interrupted sources resume only unfinished files. A file is successful after its object and metadata are persisted and vectorization is successfully dispatched; the Manifest does not wait for segmentation or vector persistence.

Other server plugins can import `knowledgeBaseManifestServiceToken` and the associated contract from `@nocobase/app-plugin-ai-knowledge-base/server`. Callers must provide both the parsed Manifest and its source so direct calls share the same persistent idempotency and recovery semantics as startup configuration. No Manifest HTTP API is provided.
Document upload is an authenticated, multipart, single-file operation for LOCAL knowledge bases. The accepted filename extensions are exactly `.pdf`, `.pptx`, `.doc`, `.docx`, `.xls`, `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.txt`, `.md`, `.json`, and `.csv`; the maximum file size is 100 MiB. The server stores the file on the disk configured for the knowledge base, creates one document, and attempts to dispatch vectorization to the asynchronous queue. It always returns that single document after successful storage; a queue-dispatch failure marks the document `ERROR` with a retryable message rather than turning the completed upload into a 500. Parsing, segmentation, embedding, and vector persistence remain asynchronous, so clients must observe document status until it reaches `SUCCESS` or `ERROR`.

Pages are not registered on the server: the client route tree lists them. Release subject registrations at shutdown.
4. Protect every server route with authentication. For a simple single-scope Repository operation, keep `defineRepositoryApiRoutes` and add `authz.database.authorizeRepository` to map methods to composite actions; it reuses or initializes the request's authorization context. For workflows, persisted-state checks, multiple data scopes or custom responses, install `authz.middleware()`, call `c.get('authz').authorize()` once and bind every returned collection policy with `repository.withPolicy()`. Follow [Repository route integration](references/repository-routes.md).
